title: JSA-CIM: A Joint-Sparse AdderNet Compute-In-Memory Accelerator for Energy-Efficient Edge AI Applications
problem: Existing CIM designs for AdderNet fail to exploit inherent model sparsity in both activations and weights, missing substantial opportunities for energy efficiency improvement in edge AI deployment.
motivation: AdderNet offers significant computational advantages over CNNs through efficient Sum-Of-Absolute-Differences operations, but realizing energy-efficient CIM deployment requires exploiting joint sparsity patterns in both activation and weight dimensions.
method: JSA-CIM is an 8T-SRAM-based digital CIM for efficient AdderNet inference exploiting joint-sparsity of activations and weights in bit-serial fashion. Architecture-level features include sparsity-aware CIM macro exploiting word-level activation sparsity; circuit-level includes novel 8T-SRAM bitline architecture exploiting both activation and bit-level weight sparsity; robust sparsity-gated minimum selection for reliable and efficient bit-serial minimum operation.
key_novelty: Joint-sparsity exploitation in both activation and weight dimensions through specialized 8T-SRAM bitline architecture for energy-efficient AdderNet CIM computation.
contributions: Sparsity and kernel-size-aware CIM macro for flexible architecture configuration and throughput optimization
Novel 8T-SRAM bitline architecture exploiting word-level activation and bit-level weight sparsity
Robust sparsity-gated minimum selection circuit for reliable bit-serial minimum operations
65nm implementation achieving 170.7 GOPS throughput, 1.8 TOPS/mm² area efficiency, 75.98 TOPS/W energy efficiency
limitations: Evaluation limited to AdderNet architecture; applicability to other sparse neural network models and scaling to larger arrays is not discussed.
primary_theme: Joint-sparsity AdderNet acceleration via specialized CIM
